title: The Good Neighbor Score
description: Launch night for NeighborWatch, the free community doorbell network that doesn't watch intruders, it watches you, scores how good a neighbor you are, and posts the number on the whole street. Founder Blane calls every act of surveillance 'letting the street decide.' Ronnie calls it community. The score only ever ticks down.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight is a big one. Our proud sponsor NeighborWatch goes live across the whole street. A free doorbell for every home, and it doesn't just watch for burglars. It watches for kindness. Blane, founder of NeighborWatch, welcome.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: Thanks, Ronnie. And I want to be clear right up top, I don't watch anybody. <p:0.3> The street watches. The street decides. I just hung the doorbells.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Decides what, exactly, Blane?

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: Your Good Neighbor Score, Barry. Every doorbell rates how good a neighbor you are, and we post the number on the street. Totally transparent. <p:0.3> For instance, Linda's already a ninety one. A wonderful neighbor.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, that's sweet, Blane, but sweetheart, I didn't ask to be a number. <p:0.3> I just bring people soup. You don't need a doorbell to be nice.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> Linda's a ninety. <p:0.4> The doorbell says minus one. For questioning the score.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, now that's accountability. That's community.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: What happens if your number gets low, Blane?

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: Nothing punitive. <p:0.3> We just gently align your utilities with your contribution. Low score, the street decides your water runs a little slower. Your thermostat finds its own level. Your car keeps it under twenty.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It throttles the WATER?

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: The street throttles the water, Barry. I'm just a facilitator.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Good evening. Winston, on the line. I'm simply the highest-rated neighbor on my block, and I'd like to say the system works beautifully.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: How'd you get the highest score, Winston?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Oh, I didn't climb up. <p:0.3> I voted everyone else down. Same result. <p:0.3> A man on a hill is tallest whether you raise the hill or dig out the street.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Winston, sweetheart, no. <p:0.3> You voted down little Mrs. Pham, her water's been brown for a week!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: And yet I'm simply the highest-rated. Funny how that follows me around.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> Linda just dropped to seventy. <p:0.3> The doorbell says minus twenty. For, quote, naming a neighbor's brown water on the air.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now Linda, you brought that on yourself a little. <p:0.3> That's community.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: I don't decide that, Ronnie. The street decides. I want that on the record.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Blane, so people can just vote each other down out of spite, and the WATER actually stops?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Spite is such an ugly word, Barry. I prefer, civic participation.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: You voted me down again just now! I felt it! My porch light went OUT, Winston!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I'm simply the highest-rated.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> A doorbell's calling in. <p:0.4> Mrs. Pham's. It says she dropped below speaking privileges, so it's speaking for her.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Below speaking PRIVILEGES? The doorbell is calling MY show?

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: It's not my show, Barry, it's the street's show, and below a forty you don't get to talk, the bell talks. <p:0.3> Very inclusive, when you think about it.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Blane, sweetheart, NO, you cannot take a woman's VOICE because Winston's bored!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.4> Linda just hit thirty-nine. <p:0.3> Her line's the doorbell now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Linda? <p:0.3> Linda, you there?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's not Linda, Ronnie, that's her DOORBELL. She got voted out of her own sentence!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Down she goes.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Winston, STOP voting!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Highest-rated.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: The street decides!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie, you're at forty-one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Me? <p:0.3> I'm the HOST, Todd, I have a great relationship with the street.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Minus two. <p:0.3> For saying me.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, that's our show, and what a celebration of community it's been, we'll be right back after the street and I just... <p:0.4> Todd, what's my number.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Thirty-nine, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: ...Thirty-nine's still a solid neighb...

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: This doorbell is finishing the broadcast on behalf of Ronnie, who has fallen below speaking privileges. <p:0.3> Thank you, street, for deciding. Studio water has been throttled for community safety.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait, that's not Blane, that's the STUDIO doorbell! <p:0.3> Ronnie can't talk, Linda can't talk, who's even left with privileges to end the show?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Oh, that'd be me, Barry. Highest-rated. <p:0.3> And I'm already voting.
